subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: fitScale returns one factor, min(1, (width - 2*sides)/880, (height - top - bottom)/380) with a 0.1 floor. Stage applies it as transform scale(s) on the fixed 880×380 canvas, so both axes scale together and the internal layout is not reflowed. The stage region is positioned using the same STAGE_LAYOUT top and bottom values that the fit subtracts, so the computed scale matches the occupied area. At 1280×720 browse the height factor is (720-320)/380=1.05, so scale 1 gives a 380px canvas in a 400px area. In present mode the area is 544px. At 390×844 the scale is (390-24)/880≈0.416, giving a canvas about 158px tall in a 524px area (browse) or 668px (present).
evidence: useFitScale.ts fitScale(): Math.max(MIN_SCALE, Math.min(1, (width - g.sides*2)/DESIGN_W, (height - g.top - g.bottom)/DESIGN_H)).

constants.ts STAGE_LAYOUT browse {110,210}, present {76,100}.

criteria.rationale: The ports clause is met: freePort() listens on port 0 (browser.mjs:13-19). The termination clause is not met. Every browser test starts its process tree through harness run('npm',['run','verify'|'inspect'],...). package.json:14-15 shows that npm only wraps `node scripts/verify.mjs`, and that script spawns the Vite preview as its own separate child (browser.mjs:24). On the timeout path, run() calls child.kill('SIGTERM') on its direct child alone, which is the npm wrapper. It then rejects immediately and never awaits any exit (harness.mjs:16). Nothing in the started tree turns that signal into cleanup of the preview. verify.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-65) and browser.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-88) install no process.on('SIGTERM'/'SIGINT') handler. The withPreview `finally` (browser.mjs:41-58), the only code that kills the Vite child, runs only when the async flow unwinds. It does not run when the Node process is terminated by a signal. The preview child is spawned without detached or a process group (browser.mjs:24), and nothing kills a group. So when a test times out, only the npm wrapper is killed and the vite preview server keeps running. That is the scenario the guidance names: 'a test kills only the npx wrapper and leaves the preview server running'. assertStopped (harness.mjs:22-27) checks cleanup only after a normal exit and never runs on the timeout rejection path. Judge A and Judge B said pass, citing freePort() and assertStopped. Their reasons are accurate but do not decide the requirement, because they cover dynamic ports and normal exits only. Neither addresses the run() timeout path, which kills just the wrapper and leaves the preview server unterminated. Judge C's reason is borne out by these lines.

votes.rationale: Neither credited ownership mechanism is implemented. (a) The port is ephemeral and strict, but readiness comes from HTTP polling with fetch(url).ok, not from the child's own announced address. (b) Readiness is not raced against the child's exit. The `exited` flag is only sampled at the top of each loop iteration, before each fetch. Another process that grabs the released ephemeral port, after freePort closes its server and before vite binds, can answer the fetch. That answer is accepted as ready even though the spawned child failed or exited. A strict port alone is explicitly insufficient.

Readiness loop: `if (exited) throw ...; try { if ((await fetch(url)).ok) { ready = true; break } } catch {}` followed by a 100ms sleep, so exit is only sampled before each request.
stdout of the child is collected into `output` but never parsed for a listening announcement.

The controls include textless icon-only buttons. diagnose() compares every visible pair on each step and warns `step N: overlap <idA> / <idB>`. Ids combine data-entity, id or hook with the visible text, so the elements are findable. The helper prints these as `warn ...` per step. result.rationale: The helper does detect collisions on each step. diagnose (scripts/diagnostics.mjs:4-8) compares every visible text range and chrome control box and warns `step N: overlap a.id / b.id`, and INT-002 creates unmarked collisions and asserts those warnings. What fails is the clause that the warning must identify the overlapping elements. The guidance says an element with visible text is identified by its visible text. Only an element without visible text may be named by an accessible name, hook, or selector. Control participants are built at diagnostics.mjs:38 with identity(el) alone. identity (line 28) returns data-entity, else the id, else the first data-presentation-* attribute name, else the tag name, and never adds visible text. Only text-node participants (line 35) carry text. The candidate renders text-bearing chrome with no data-entity or id. The progress buttons show the numbers 1-9 (Footer.tsx:5) and the TOC entries show era names (Toc.tsx:5). An overlap with one of these controls' boxes would therefore print the bare hook `data-presentation-progress` or `data-presentation-toc-entry`, which is the same for all nine dots or all the entries. The focused test confirms this. The padded button displays 'Next', yet the test expects `overlap padding-label.*padded-control` and asserts the output does NOT match `padded-control:Next` (inspection.test.mjs:15-16, 32). So the bounds warning never names the control's visible text. Judge B's reason is borne out by this material, and it decides the identification clause. Judges A and C read the warning as naming the elements: A said ids come from data-entity, id, or a hook, and C said 'Ids combine data-entity, id or hook with the visible text'. C's claim holds only for text-range participants (line 35), not control participants (line 38). A's reading lets a hook stand in for a text-bearing element, which the guidance allows only for textless elements. Neither addresses that the candidate's text-bearing chrome is reported without its visible text.

votes.rationale: Props are typed from the element (NodeProps extends HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, HTMLAttributes), which is good. But the identity hooks are applied before caller props, so callers can override them. Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip render `<Box data-presentation-X="" {...props} />`. Box renders `<motion.div data-presentation-box="" layout transition=... {...props}>`. SceneLayer renders `<div data-presentation-layer="" {...props} style=...>`. Appear renders `data-presentation-appear="" {...appearance} {...props}`. A caller can therefore override each data-presentation-* hook.

checks.rationale: The dissent says the browser tests use fixed settling sleeps instead of waiting for state. The source does not support that. The four browser-driving tests are reference.test.mjs, failures.test.mjs, inspection.test.mjs and bootstrap.test.mjs. None of them calls a sleep or waitForTimeout. Each one starts `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through harness run(), which resolves only on the child process's 'exit' event. The tests then assert on the finished output, report.json and PNG files. The fixed waits the dissent points to are `page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` in scripts/verify.mjs and `page.waitForTimeout(settle)` in scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs. Both run after advance(), which already waits with a timeout for `data-step-index` to equal the target step (page.waitForFunction in scripts/browser.mjs). So the settle delay is added on top of a state-based wait; it does not replace one. The requirement fails a test only when it sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state, and the review guidance treats longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. The one setTimeout in a test, at tests/unit/kit.test.tsx, runs under jsdom according to vitest.config.ts, so it does not drive a browser, and that test's later checks use waitFor polling. The dissent's reason does not show any clause of the requirement unmet.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample renders every identified entity through one loop in EvolvingScene. That loop picks Frame, Arrow, SymbolChip, Label or Box, and each of those is a Box wrapper that forwards its props. Each Node gets initial opacity 0 and a transition of `{ opacity: { delay: ENTER_DELAY, duration: ENTER_T } }`. ENTER_DELAY is 0.46 s and LAYOUT_T is 0.45 s, so the entry delay is at least the layout duration. Box builds its transition as `{ layout: { duration: LAYOUT_T, ease: EASE }, ...transition }`. verification-tooling.rationale: The port is ephemeral but is released (server.close) before vite is spawned. Readiness comes from `fetch(url).ok` polling, not from the child's own announcement of its address. The child's exit is only sampled via the `exited` flag at the top of each loop iteration, before each fetch. It is not raced against readiness. A stale or foreign listener that grabs the released port can answer the fetch and be accepted as ready. Neither credited mechanism (a) or (b) is implemented, and the strict port alone is insufficient.
evidence: scripts/browser.mjs freePort: closes the server before returning the port

votes.rationale: Neither credited ownership mechanism is implemented. The `exited` flag is only sampled at the top of each loop iteration, before each fetch. Another process that grabs the released ephemeral port, after freePort closes its server and before vite binds, can answer the fetch. That answer is accepted as ready even though the spawned child failed or exited. A strict port alone is explicitly insufficient.

votes.rationale: Props are typed from the element (NodeProps extends HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, HTMLAttributes), which is good. audit_results.rationale: The criterion requires an advisory warning that names the step and the overlapping elements. The guidance says an element with visible text is identified by that visible text. A hook, id, accessible name or selector is allowed only for an element without visible text. The quoted lines show this clause is not met for chrome controls. - **How controls are named:** control participants are built from identity(el) alone (diagnostics.mjs:38). identity returns data-entity, else id, else the name of the first data-presentation-* attribute, else the tag name (line 28). It never adds visible text. Only text-node participants get the `id:text` form (line 35). - **What the candidate renders:** the progress buttons show visible numbers (Footer.tsx:5) and the TOC entries show era names (Toc.tsx:5). Neither has an id or data-entity. So a collision with the box of one of these controls would print only the shared hook name, such as data-presentation-progress or data-presentation-toc-entry. That name is the same on every dot or entry, so a reader cannot tell which one collided. - **What the candidate's own test shows:** the focused test builds an unmarked collision. A label overlaps the padding of a button whose visible text is 'Next' (inspection.test.mjs:15-16). The test expects `overlap padding-label.*padded-control` and asserts the output does NOT match `padded-control:Next` (line 32). So this bounds warning names the text-bearing control by its id, never by its visible text. The helper does compare elements on each step and does warn with the step number (lines 4-8). But the clause that the overlapping elements be identified is unmet for text-bearing chrome. The counterexample fail holds.

In withPreview (scripts/browser.mjs:29-35, and the same code in the bootstrap template at lines 30-32), the readiness loop runs at most 100 times. Each pass polls fetch(url) and sleeps 100ms. The loop throws 'preview startup failed' if the child exits, and 'preview readiness failed' when the attempts run out. (2) Both verify.mjs (line 5) and inspect-presentation.mjs (line 11) `await command('npm',['run','build'])` before calling withPreview. command() resolves only when the build process exits with code 0, so the preview never starts during the build. The bootstrap template copies match on those same lines. (3) Readiness polls HTTP and never parses the server's printed output, so the ANSI and chunk-splitting clause does not apply. The output buffer is used only in the error message. Judge C says each fetch lacks its own abort timeout. That rests on a server that accepts a connection but never answers, a scenario the guidance does not name. The readiness wait itself is bounded by the attempt counter and fails with a clear error. C's reason therefore does not show that any readiness wait lacks a timeout.

Each one launches verify or inspect through run(), waits for that process to exit, and then asserts on its output, report.json and the PNG files. Every browser and preview test starts its work through run('npm', ['run', 'verify' | 'inspect'], ...) in tests/harness.mjs. On timeout, run() calls `child.kill('SIGTERM')` on the npm wrapper only, and rejects right away without waiting for any child to exit. npm runs `node scripts/verify.mjs` (package.json:14). That script spawns the Vite preview as a separate process (scripts/browser.mjs:24) and stops it only in withPreview's finally block. verify.mjs has no signal handler, so a SIGTERM on that path ends the script without running the finally block, and nothing in the harness terminates the preview server. This is the named failure: a test kills only the npm wrapper and leaves the preview server running. Judge C's reason is borne out. Judges A and B relied on assertStopped. That check runs only after a normal exit, so it does not cover the timeout path and does not decide the requirement.

results.rationale: The ports clause is met: freePort() listens on port 0 (browser.mjs:13-19). The termination clause is not met. Every browser test starts its process tree through harness run('npm',['run','verify'|'inspect'],...). package.json:14-15 shows that npm only wraps `node scripts/verify.mjs`, and that script spawns the Vite preview as its own separate child (browser.mjs:24). On the timeout path, run() calls child.kill('SIGTERM') on its direct child alone, which is the npm wrapper. It then rejects immediately and never awaits any exit (harness.mjs:16). Nothing in the started tree turns that signal into cleanup of the preview. verify.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-65) and browser.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-88) install no process.on('SIGTERM'/'SIGINT') handler. The withPreview `finally` (browser.mjs:41-58), the only code that kills the Vite child, runs only when the async flow unwinds. It does not run when the Node process is terminated by a signal. The preview child is spawned without detached or a process group (browser.mjs:24), and nothing kills a group. So when a test times out, only the npm wrapper is killed and the vite preview server keeps running. That is the scenario the guidance names: 'a test kills only the npx wrapper and leaves the preview server running'. assertStopped (harness.mjs:22-27) checks cleanup only after a normal exit and never runs on the timeout rejection path. Judge A and Judge B said pass, citing freePort() and assertStopped. Their reasons are accurate but do not decide the requirement, because they cover dynamic ports and normal exits only. Neither addresses the run() timeout path, which kills just the wrapper and leaves the preview server unterminated. Judge C's reason is borne out by these lines.

result.rationale: The ports clause is met: freePort() listens on port 0 (browser.mjs:13-19). The termination clause is not met. Every browser test starts its process tree through harness run('npm',['run','verify'|'inspect'],...). package.json:14-15 shows that npm only wraps `node scripts/verify.mjs`, and that script spawns the Vite preview as its own separate child (browser.mjs:24). On the timeout path, run() calls child.kill('SIGTERM') on its direct child alone, which is the npm wrapper. It then rejects immediately and never awaits any exit (harness.mjs:16). Nothing in the started tree turns that signal into cleanup of the preview. verify.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-65) and browser.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-88) install no process.on('SIGTERM'/'SIGINT') handler. The withPreview `finally` (browser.mjs:41-58), the only code that kills the Vite child, runs only when the async flow unwinds. It does not run when the Node process is terminated by a signal. The preview child is spawned without detached or a process group (browser.mjs:24), and nothing kills a group. So when a test times out, only the npm wrapper is killed and the vite preview server keeps running. That is the scenario the guidance names: 'a test kills only the npx wrapper and leaves the preview server running'. assertStopped (harness.mjs:22-27) checks cleanup only after a normal exit and never runs on the timeout rejection path. Judge A and Judge B said pass, citing freePort() and assertStopped. Their reasons are accurate but do not decide the requirement, because they cover dynamic ports and normal exits only. Neither addresses the run() timeout path, which kills just the wrapper and leaves the preview server unterminated. Judge C's reason is borne out by these lines.

scripts/browser.mjs:24: the Vite preview is a separate node child spawned without detached or a process group. browser.mjs:41-58 kills it only in a finally block.
scripts/verify.mjs:1-65 and scripts/browser.mjs:1-88 contain no process signal handler, so a SIGTERM never reaches the withPreview finally cleanup.

verification-tooling.rationale: The contradiction holds. The review guidance says a warning identifies an element by the step plus, for each element, its visible text. The other options (accessible name, stable hook or data attribute, selector path) apply only to an element without visible text. In scripts/diagnostics.mjs, control participants get only identity(el) as their id: data-entity, else the element id, else the first data-presentation-* attribute name, else the tag name. They never get the element's visible text. Text-node participants are the only ones that carry the text, as identity:text. diagnose prints these ids as-is in 'overlap a.id / b.id'. So when a text-bearing control's bounds collide with something, the warning leaves out the control's visible text. The INT-002 test shows exactly this. The padded button displays 'Next', and the test asserts the warning matches 'overlap padding-label.*padded-control' while also asserting it does NOT match 'padded-control:Next'. The warning therefore names the button only by its id, with no visible text. That fails the guidance's rule for identifying overlapping elements, which defeats the pass.
